name: Workers' compensation
what: Insure employees under the workers' compensation scheme of each state where they work, or self-insure.

basis.source: 5-year Productivity Inquiry: A more productive labour market (volume 7)
basis.quote: with the exception of Comcare, workers compensation schemes are operated at a state level. As there are differences between states for insurance requirements and workers compensation eligibility

issues.what: Each state runs its own workers' compensation scheme, with different definitions of a worker, benefits, return-to-work rules and reporting, so national employers comply with each.

evidence.source: Annual Review of Regulatory Burdens on Business: Manufacturing and Distributive Trades
evidence.quote: Numerous inconsistencies exist across State, Territory and Commonwealth Workers Compensation Legislation. Woolworths, as a national operator, must comply with each of the regulations in the States and Territories in which it operates, which is costly and time consuming.

the lack of harmonisation across state and territory workplace safety frameworks, particularly with respect to workers compensation, increases compliance costs and administrative complexity for companies operating across borders

issues.what: Whether a contractor counts as a 'deemed worker' depends on the state.

evidence.source: 5-year Productivity Inquiry: A more productive labour market (volume 7)
evidence.quote: A limited set of independent contractors are covered under 'deemed worker' provisions in workers compensation legislation, although coverage differs by state and territory.
